Article Title: Amid disruption, Lok Sabha passes 2 more bills sans debate
Article Text:
Since the monsoon session began, nine of 11 bills were passed in the lower House without a discussion

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha Tuesday passed two more bills — one on renaming Kerala as Keralam and the other that seeks to broaden the mandate of National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) to give loans and grants directly to cooperative societies — without discussion as opposition members continued with their protests and sloganeering demanding the presence of home minister Amit Shah in the House.Carrying placards to the well of the House, Samajwadi Party members raised slogans against Shah and the embezzlement of Ram temple donations.Since the monsoon session began, nine of 11 bills were passed in the lower House without a discussion. The House could not even complete question hour in the session which is scheduled to conclude Thursday.Moving the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026, for passing, MoS for home affairs Nityanand Rai took a swipe at the main opposition party which governs Kerala, saying it seemed Congress MPs were not in favour of the renaming. Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju also took a dig at Congress, saying he was saddened that party MP K C Venugopal, who is elected from Kerala, could not speak on the bill.The National Cooperative Development Corporation (Amendment) Bill was moved by MoS for cooperation Murlidhar Mohol. Both bills were listed in the name of Shah. In his absence, the bills were moved by junior ministers. The bills are now expected to go to RS for consideration Wednesday.When proceedings of the House began, Speaker Om Birla expressed anguish over repeated disruptions and appealed to govt and opposition to arrive at a common ground. As the stalemate continued, he adjourned the proceedings. TNN
Article Summary: Since the monsoon session began, nine of 11 bills were passed in the lower House without a discussion. Opposition members continued with their protests and sloganeering demanding the presence of home minister Amit Shah in the House. The House could not even complete question hour in the session which is scheduled to conclude Thursday.

Article Title: Probe Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das others over presence of minors at Delhi protest: 'Mumbai influencer' to cops
Article Text:
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, chief spokesperson Saurav Das and national spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka.





MUMBAI: A Mumbai resident claiming to be a social media influencer has filed a complaint with the Indore police, seeking an investigation into the alleged presence of minor boys and girls at a recent students' protest led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in New Delhi.The complaint was filed with the city crime branch on Wednesday and seeks an investigation into the alleged role of CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, chief spokesperson Saurav Das and others in the participation of minors at the protest at Jantar Mantar.The complainant, Faizan Ansari, alleged that the probe should determine whether Dipke, Das or others were involved in bringing, inviting, encouraging or facilitating the participation of minors in the protest held over the NEET question paper leak case.He also sought the preservation and examination of photographs and videos from the protest, media interviews, public statements, CCTV footage from the protest site and surrounding areas, social media posts and other electronic records.The complaint stated that if the investigation establishes any cognizable offence under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the Information Technology Act or the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, an FIR should be registered against those involved.Additional deputy commissioner of Police Rajesh Dandotiya said, "We have received a complaint from Ansari, who claims to be a social media influencer. The complaint is being investigated. Appropriate action will be taken based on the facts that emerge from the investigation."The CJP-led youth protest at Jantar Mantar over the NEET question paper leak lasted 36 days and ended with the resignation of then-Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.On July 20, when protesters attempted to march towards Parliament, Delhi Police stopped them and used force to disperse the demonstrators, leading to clashes between the two sides.The CJP withdrew its protest on July 25 after Pradhan's resignation and talks with the government, which accepted the demands raised by the agitators.
Article Summary: A Mumbai resident claims to be a social media influencer. He has filed a complaint with the Indore police, seeking an investigation into the alleged presence of minor boys and girls at a recent students' protest. The complaint was filed with the city crime branch on Wednesday.

Article Title: Maharashtra government approves withdrawal of cases against CJP-supported protesters
Article Text:
File pic of protesters at Shivaji Park in support of the CJP-led agitation in Delhi against the NEET paper leak

Mumbai:





The Maharashtra government on Wednesday issued a Government Resolution (GR) approving the withdrawal of cases registered against students and protesters supporting the Cockroach Janta Party-led agitations over the NEET paper leak.The GR stated that these cases, including those related to political protests, will be eligible for withdrawal where chargesheets are to be filed up to March 31, 2027, extending the earlier deadline of July 31, 2026.Police file chargesheets before the court in the registered FIRs after completing the investigation.The state home department was compiling details of all such cases registered against the CJP-supported protests across the state, mainly in Mumbai. The government can withdraw registered police cases only after a chargesheet is filed or after police submits closure report in court.Thousands of students had participated in protests across Maharashtra demanding Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan ’s resignation after the NEET paper leak. Over seven days beginning July 18, Mumbai Police filed 16 FIRs for unlawful assembly under Section 189(2) of BNS and for violating prohibitory orders under Sections 37(1), 37(3) and 135 of the Maharashtra Police Act.Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis had recently asked additional chief secretary (home) Manisha Mhaiskar to initiate the process of withdrawing the cases registered against protesters at CJP-led agitations.
Article Summary: Government Resolution (GR) approving the withdrawal of cases registered against students and protesters supporting Cockroach Janta Party-led agitations over the NEET paper leak. Thousands of students had participated in protests across Maharashtra demanding Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan ’s resignation.

Article Title: Driver approached with bribe to murder BJP MLA; 2 booked
Article Text:
Kolhapur

:





A case has been registered against two individuals for allegedly offering a cash bribe to the driver of BJP MLA Sachin Kalyanshetti to kill him.According to the complaint filed by the MLA’s driver, Anand Survase, the accused approached him on Aug 7 around 4pm near Mahavir Chowk in Solapur and explicitly offered him money to shoot the MLA dead, assuring him that they would “handle the rest” afterwards.On the basis of this complaint, an FIR under sections 55 (abetment of an offence punishable with death or life imprisonment where the main offence is not committed) and 3(5) (common intention) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita was registered at Sadar Bazaar police station on Monday. However, no arrests have been made so far.The driver had accompanied the wife and son of the sitting MLA for shopping at a shoe showroom. While the driver was waiting outside the showroom, the two suspects approached him.“One of the suspects offered money to the complainant and instigated him by saying they will give him money. They asked him to shoot and kill the MLA and they will handle what comes thereafter,” a police officer said.The case is now being investigated by an assistant police inspector. Kalyanshetti declined to comment on the possible motive behind the alleged attempt. “Let the police carry out the investigation,” he said.Meanwhile, hundreds of Kalyanshetti’s supporters met Solapur commissioner of police M Rajkumar on Tuesday demanding a detailed probe.
Article Summary: A case has been registered against two individuals for allegedly offering a cash bribe to the driver of BJP MLA Sachin Kalyanshetti to kill him. According to the complaint filed by the MLA’s driver, Anand Survase, the accused approached him on Aug 7 around 4pm near Mahavir Chowk.

Article Title: Elderly siblings killed in accident in Pargaon
Article Text:
Pune:





Two siblings, aged 58 and 60, were killed after a pick-up truck hit their two-wheeler in Pargaon near Daund on Tuesday evening. They were returning home after visiting their grandson, who’d been injured earlier in an accident when the tragedy struck, Pune Rural police said.The deceased were identified as Subhadra Shitole (60) and Mohan Takawane (58), both residents of Pargaon’s Takawane Vasti.“Around 4pm, when they neared their home, a pick-up truck hit their motorcycle. Both sufferd severe injuries in the accident,” the officer said.They were taken to a nearby hospital, where doctors pronounced them dead, he said. The police have registered a case of causing death by negligence against the pick-up truck driver, he added.
Article Summary: Two siblings, aged 58 and 60, were killed after a pick-up truck hit their two- wheeler in Pargaon near Daund. They were returning home after visiting their grandson, who'd been injured earlier in an accident when the tragedy struck.

Article Title: Big reforms in recruitment exams: Maha sets up panel
Article Text: Nagpur: Seeking to restore confidence in govt recruitment examinations after a series of controversies over paper leaks and malpractices across the country, Maharashtra on Wednesday announced a comprehensive overhaul of its recruitment examination system by constituting a high-level committee to recommend structural reforms.Chairing a special meeting in Mumbai, chief minister Devendra Fadnavis directed that the committee undertake extensive consultations with students, educational institutions and other stakeholders across every revenue division before submitting a comprehensive report that will shape the state's future recruitment examination policy. Deputy CM Eknath Shinde also attended the meeting and offered suggestions on the proposed reforms.The committee will be headed by addl chief secretary (general administration) V Radha and include director general of police Sadanand Date, information technology secretary Virendra Singh, animal husbandry secretary N Ramaswamy and Nashik divisional commissioner Pravin Gedam.The move follows growing public demand for transparent and tamper-proof recruitment processes after repeated allegations of paper leaks in competitive exams across several states.Maharashtra has already initiated broader recruitment reforms, including a phased transition to computer-based examinations from Aug 2027.The govt will also create at least 25,000 secure classrooms equipped to conduct recruitment examinations under enhanced surveillance and monitoring protocols, govt sources said.The meeting also reviewed the coordination among district collectors, police commissioners, superintendents of police and senior education officials.
Article Summary: The move follows growing public demand for transparent and tamper-proof recruitment processes. There have been repeated allegations of paper leaks in competitive exams across several states. The govt will also create at least 25,000 secure classrooms equipped to conduct recruitment examinations under enhanced surveillance and monitoring protocols.

Article Title: 2 Bangladeshi nationals held for illegal entry
Article Text:
Nashik:

TOI





The crime branch (unit 2) of Nashik city police arrested two Bangladeshi nationals who illegally entered India and were preparing to travel to Pune via Nashik.Acting on the directives of commissioner of police Sandeep Karnik and DCP (crime) Kiran Kumar Chavan to track foreign nationals staying illegally in the city, head constables Pradeep Nannavare and Santosh Supekar, in the course of gathering information, had received confidential intelligence regarding the suspects.The informer told the police that a man and a woman, both Bangladeshi nationals, had infiltrated into India and were present at the Nashik Road bus stand to catch a bus to Pune. Soon after getting the information, the constables contacted their senior officials, after which a team was prepared and a trap was laid near the police chowky at the Nashik Road bus stand. The suspects were later arrested.They have been identified as Mohammad Sakib Mulla (22) and Nahida Badshah Mulla (29), both from Narail district in Khulna state of Bangladesh.Upon questioning, neither of them could produce valid travel documents or passports and confessed to crossing the India-Bangladesh border illegally.A case has been registered at the Nashik Road police Station on behalf of govt following a complaint filed by Supekar.Chavan, while talking to, said people from Bangladesh generally intrude into India to seek employment. “Nonetheless, the case is being investigated,” he said.
Article Summary: Two Bangladeshi nationals illegally entered India and were preparing to travel to Pune via Nashik. Mohammad Sakib Mulla and Nahida Badshah Mulla, both from Narail district in Khulna state of Bangladesh, were arrested.

Article Title: Bike mechanic arrested again for molesting techie
Article Text:
Busted

Chennai:





Thoraipakkam police arrested a 31-year-old bike mechanic on Tuesday for sexually harassing a 22-year-old woman near a private college bus stop on Rajiv Gandhi Salai. The accused was produced before a court and remanded to judicial custody. Police identified the accused as Manikandan , a resident of Thoraipakkam. The complainant, a 22-year-old woman from Madurai district, works at an IT company in Chennai. Article Title: Cop arrested for accepting Rs 30,000 bribe from farmer near Namakkal
Article Text:
Representative image





NAMAKKAL: Sleuths of the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) have arrested a special sub-inspector (SSI) attached to Nallur police station in Namakkal district on charges of accepting a bribe of Rs 30,000 to settle a land encroachment case.SSI V Gangadharan demanded Rs 30,000 from K Saumiyaraj, 47, a farmer in Nadandhai Salappalayam, to close a land encroachment case registered against him and his neighbour, S Muthusamy, 48, four months ago.Unwilling to pay the bribe, Saumiyaraj lodged a complaint with the DVAC unit in Namakkal on Tuesday. Acting on the complaint, officials instructed him to hand over chemical-coated currency notes to the tune of Rs 30,000 to the SSI.On Tuesday evening, as Saumiyaraj handed over the cash to Gangadharan, DVAC sleuths led by inspector Prabhu caught him red-handed. “He was arrested and taken into custody for interrogation,” said a DVAC officer.
Article Summary: SSI V Gangadharan demanded Rs 30,000 from K Saumiyaraj, 47, a farmer in Nadandhai Salappalayam. DVAC sleuths led by inspector Prabhu caught him red- handed.

Article Title: Inspectors’ lapses lead to series of acquittals
Article Text:
Magistrate said an inspector had “merely acted as a postman” by filing the final report after a sub-inspector conducted the investigation





Madurai: From being criticised for failing to investigate cases themselves to admitting they did not know what had happened in their own stations, it has been a rough two weeks for police inspectors appearing before Madurai courts. In one case, a magistrate said an inspector had “merely acted as a postman” by filing the final report after a sub-inspector conducted the investigation.The remark came in a fatal accident case involving Sayyid Ibrahim Badusha. Police alleged that he drove a cab into a two-wheeler ridden by Kavin on Madurai-Azhagarkovil Road on Feb 3, 2023. Kavin suffered injuries and died at Government Rajaji Hospital on Feb 6.Judicial magistrate D Lakshmi Priya found that sub-inspector Govindaraju had conducted the investigation, though an Inspector should have handled the fatal accident case. Inspector Palraju later took over but did not conduct further investigation to establish the accident spot or negligence. It held that these lapses weakened the prosecution case leading to acquittal of the accused.A similar lapse surfaced in a 2019 illegal mining case from Peraiyur. Police accused S Ashok Kumar of transporting one unit of bar soil in a tractor with an unregistered trailer near S Melapatti on July 22, 2019.Sub-inspector Mahendhiran seized the vehicle and registered the case. Inspector Gandhi later examined the case records and filed the private complaint.The MMDR court noted that govt orders authorised only police officers not below Inspector rank to seize minerals and vehicles under the Act. Since Mahendhiran was an SI, the court held that he was not authorised to make the seizure. It also cited contradictions over the alleged sand and acquitted Ashok Kumar.The third setback came in a ganja case registered by Vedasandur police in 2020. Police alleged that D Selvi and P Poonkodi possessed 3kg of ganja. Sub-inspector Jesu Rajangam led the raid, while inspector Kavitha later took over the investigation and filed the final report.During cross-examination, Kavitha admitted she had no direct knowledge of the incident. The court found no documentary proof that the secret information was recorded or that permission was obtained before the raid. It also found that seized ganja reached court only on March 5, 2020, after its Jan 24 seizure, with no safe-custody record for the intervening period. Finding violations of mandatory NDPS procedures, the court acquitted the accused.
Article Summary: Magistrate said an inspector had ‘merely acted as a postman’ by filing the final report after a sub-inspector conducted the investigation. The remark came in a fatal accident case involving Sayyid Ibrahim Badusha. A similar lapse surfaced in a 2019 illegal mining case from Peraiyur.

Article Title: 13-year-old boy’s death: Family alleges medical negligence
Article Text:
accident

Theni:





The mother of a 13-year-old boy who died after undergoing treatment at government hospitals in Theni district has lodged a police complaint alleging medical negligence and seeking action against those responsible.According to a complaint lodged with Thenkarai police, Sudha of Periyakulam alleged that her son Nivas was admitted to Periyakulam government headquarters hospital on June 3 for nasal surgery.She alleged that on June 6, complications began after an anaesthesia was wrongly administered at the hospital. The surgery was not performed, and the boy was shifted to Theni Government Medical College Hospital.Nivas remained on ventilator support in the ICU for more than two months before dying on Monday. Sudha sought action against those responsible, alleging medical negligence, and demanded a videographed postmortem by a special medical team.An internal medical committee conducted an inquiry into the incident.
Article Summary: Nivas was admitted to Periyakulam government headquarters hospital on June 3 for nasal surgery. Complications began on June 6 after an anaesthesia was wrongly administered. The boy was shifted to Theni Government Medical College Hospital. He remained on ventilator support in the ICU for more than two months before dying on Monday.

Article Title: Truck driver dies in road accident near Salem
Article Text: SALEM: A driver died in an accident involving a truck, a pickup van and a bus near Mecheri in Salem district on Wednesday. More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident.According to the Mecheri police, a TNSTC bus carrying 51 passengers was heading to Karur from Mettur when a speeding pickup van attempted to overtake it. “The pickup van collided head-on with a truck coming from the opposite direction,” said an officer at the Mecheri police station. The truck grazed the bus, shattering its windows and injuring more than 10 passengers seated near the windows.Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. The injured were rushed to govt hospitals in Mettur and Omalur.Fire service personnel, assisted by Mecheri police and residents, worked to move the damaged truck and pickup van to the roadside. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.The Mecheri police registered a case.
Article Summary: More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident. Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.

Article Title: Kerala HC impleads National Commission for Scheduled Tribes in Kumbh Mela girl case
Article Text:
Kochi

:





The high court has impleaded the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes in a police protection petition filed by the ‘viral Kumbh Mela girl’, in which she has also challenged the commission’s directive to the state police chief to hand her over to the Madhya Pradesh police.A bench of Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas issued the directive and adjourned the petition to Sept 8. The court also impleaded the state police chief, Kochi city police commissioner, SHO of Thampanoor police station and Poovar panchayat as parties and issued notices to them.Previously, the court had directed the police to provide adequate protection to the girl and directed the state govt to ensure that she was not taken outside the jurisdiction of Kochi police against her will and without further orders from the court. The order came after the court took note of a directive issued by the national commission to hand over the girl to the Madhya Pradesh police on a petition filed by a social worker concerning the petitioner’s inter-religious marriage and alleging that she was a minor at the time of the marriage.In her interlocutory application challenging the national commission’s directive, the girl contended that the commission had visited the Poovar panchayat, where her marriage to an actor from Madhya Pradesh, was registered, and verified the documents.Despite being aware that the allegation that she was a minor at the time of her marriage was false, the commission issued the directive, allegedly due to political intervention or some other pressure, she contended. She also contended that she had not been served with any order of the national commission and that taking her to her native place could expose her to the risk of “honour killing”.The girl’s marriage was solemnised at a temple in Thiruvananthapuram and subsequently registered under the Special Marriage Act on March 11. Meanwhile, the Madhya Pradesh police registered a case based on a complaint filed by the girl’s father, alleging that his daughter was abducted and she was a minor at the time of her marriage.
Article Summary: The high court has impleaded the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes in a police protection petition filed by the ‘viral Kumbh Mela girl’ She has also challenged the commission’s directive to the state police chief to hand her over to the Madhya Pradesh police. A bench of Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas issued the directive.
